Zuma's biggest blunder

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Further information:
ZUMA’S BIGGEST BLUNDER FRIDAY SCRIPT

Commentary One
Last week ANC stalwart Ben Turok flew home, picked up a paper at the airport and discovered that President Zuma had sacked Finance minister Nhlanle Nene

BEN TUROK
I could hardly believe it, and I had to read several paragraphs and I was shocked and frankly upset know him well, He is a decent man of integrity -very hard working

Commentary Two
Nene’s replacement Des Van Rooyen, pulled from the back benches of the ANC is also well known to him

John:
When you heard that he had been elevated to the position what was your response

Ben Turok
Irritation and disbelief…Because I have had a lot to do with him …economic cluster in parliament / Every time I asked him if we could discuss something serious ..whole parliamentary life working …he never said anything memorable that I can remember

Commentary Three
And says Turok even his academic background wouldn’t have been enough

Ben
No ways! No experience- It’s the same as Phiyega…honestly I think its irresponsible

Link
No matter how bad the news gets – we have always known that the treasury was sacrosanct – well minister Nene’s removal as the gatekeeper, signalled a line had been crossed and it evoked fury across South Africa

Up sound
My message to you Mr president we are tired and to the NEC stop protecting Zuma! We see you – we put you there and we are going to take you out of there!

Commentary Four
Business Day Editor Songezo Zibi

Songezo Zibi
So there have been rumours for months that the treasury reigned in because it is a law until itself – the only reason is because it holds the line –what the president did is to demonstrate that the treasury can be attacked and after that we only have the reserve bank and there will be nothing left afterwards

Commentary Five
Enough is enough, said enraged South Africans. #zumamustfall, became a rousing chorus on social media that later spilled out onto the streets

Vox One
We have a simple message for JZ and the message is this: “The country more important than the party!”

Commentary six
Minister Nene had stood up to SAA board chairperson Dudu Myeni – friend of the president and head of the Jacob Zuma foundation. She refused to accept an airbus swop arrangement that he had signed off. He sent a letter warning that failure to do the deal by 21st of this month would be considered financial misconduct. Shortly afterwards he was out

Bongani
How much pressure was Minister Nene under?
Songezo
He was under enormous pressure – SAA was simply the straw that broke the camels back

Link
The real reasons for minister Nene’s removal have not been revealed – was it his ultimatum to the president’s friend at SAA – was it the nuclear procurement deal? Either way – few believe the official line – that he was freed up for the BRICS bank position

Commentary Seven
Nene had also publicly stated that the nuclear procurement would not go ahead if we couldn’t afford it. Only hours before he was sacked – the cabinet approved the nuclear procurement process without a cost benefit analysis.

Songezo
This is going to cost us upwards of 1.5 trillion now if there is no money for SAA where are we going to get money for nuclear

Commentary eight
Yet in his post cabinet briefing to journalists Jeff Radebe failed to mention the cabinet approval for the procurement process to begin

Bongani
Why did Minister Radebe not mention that cabinet had signed off on the nuclear build programme

Songezo
It’s a helluva thing to forget! I don’t think he forgot by the way – I think
They understood fully well that the consequent question would be where will you get the money, and there would be no answers

Commentary nine
He also punches holes in the Presidents BRICS Bank explanation

SONGEZO
That statement is nonsense it appears that in this instance one of the requirements for the job is that you are unemployed – we are two months away from the next budget – who removes a finance minister for a position that wont be filled until after that. But there is another thing Bongani – the board of the development bank has not approved the position – no other country that has nominated anyone for this position – and so the president selling us a story

Commentary ten
A story no one believed – especially the markets. Economist George Glynos was astounded and watched the rand dive almost 10% and savings wiped out overnight

George
Just looking at the numbers on the JSE and the Bond market you could come up with figures north of R200 billion that was wiped off in the space of a couple of days, and lets make this real for people – these losses weren’t sustained by gungho traders and hedge fund managers – speculate – we are speaking about real people through pension funds that will have taken a helluva beating

Commentary eleven
Now we speak in Nkandlas- another analyst calculated that in only two days R500billion was wiped out of the economy– that is 2000 Nkandlas, one Nkandla every day for the next five years.

Commentary twelve
Minister Lindiwe Zulu is on the National working committee that has come out defending the president

Bongani
Minister the ANC has defended this decision …can only be valid if they are rational?

Lindiwe Zulu
Yes this was a rational decision …because once the president had indicated opportunity of Nene going to BRICS bank that is a serious position – but its his prerogative because what are you a president if you cant take decisions




George
It might have been his prerogative but it doesn’t make it the right decision. It was just bad it was catastrophic – when real losses are being suffered by real people because of ineptitude at the highest level – I don’t think that is forgivable and so accountability needs to be had in this instance, and I would like it in the form of the president stepping down.

Commentary thirteen
Ben Turok was one of a small handful of ANC heavyweights to make a similar call

Ben
I said he has a nice house in Nkandla with a swimming pool and he must go there and have a nice retirement

Commentary Fourteen
And that was the message on the streets on Reconciliation day. In Cape Town Mpho Tutu relayed her famous father’s sentiments

Mpho TUTU
He is saddened by the events of the last few weeks and the callous disregard for public good that is demonstrated by this administration

Vavi Up sound at march
We are up to here with their corruption – destroying the future of our children and our country 10 56 19

Commentary fifteen
Zwelenzima Vavi was one of several eminent persons to sign an open letter to the President

Why did you do sign the letter?
Vavi
Anybody who keeps quiet is effectively endorsing the crisis at hand
Bongani
As somebody who has a good idea of what the President thinks …when he made the decision what was he thinking?

Vavi
He is too powerful, his people love him, only a few cleva blacks will raise fingers, there will be a small hue and cry it will die down – it will be business as usual- to me this is a new ZUMA altogether

Commentary sixteen
But as a market bloodbath unfolded, the ANC remained largely silent

Songezo
The ANC for days was paralysed! And they waited for public and market backlash to build up to help them to communicate their displeasure to the president- if it is paralysed from intervening in critical moments like this – you have to ask how much capacity they actually have if its own governance appears to be captured by interests outside of the ANC?

Commentary seventeen
Songezo points to the Gupta’s

Songezo 02 55 33 ***
When a president is captured it means they become the de facto president and start appointing people in cabinet and into SOE and as Director Generals. That relationship is a danger to the stability and security of this country

Commentary eighteen
Zwelenzima Vavi agrees

Vavi
I think the power of the ministers has been eroded over time by the Gupta factor behind the scenes/ Remember some ministers have come out to say I learned about my appointment through the Guptas. I think we have a dual power situation here



SONGEZO ZIBI
There is no more space for mistakes Bongani no more space for arrogance for miscalculations – because when that happens we go to junk status and a lot of people in this country don’t remember when interest rates were 23% - you do not want junk status in this country Bongani.

End Commentary
On Friday the Mail and Guardian reported that Lindiwe Zulu said business was in a plot against Zuma, a statement Songezo described as delusional.
The rand remained uncomfortably north of R15 to the dollar and the ANC reaffirmed the president would not be recalled

The End

Last week ANC stalwart Ben Turok flew home, picked up a paper at the airport and read the news that had shocked South Africa

President
I have decided to remove Minister Nhalanhle Nene as minister of Finance…to another strategic position

BEN TUROK
I could hardly believe it, and I had to read several paragraphs and I was shocked and frankly upset know him well, He is a decent man of integrity -very hard working

Commentary Two
Nene’s replacement Des Van Rooyen, an ANC backbencher was also the convener of the economic cluster in parliament

John:
When you heard that he had been elevated to the position what was your response

Ben Turok
Disbelief and Irritation, even annoyance because I have had a lot to do with Des Van Rooyen. It was clear to me that he spent his whole parliamentary life working on his studies instead of on parliament.

Commentary Three
Van Rooyen has a masters degree in finance but that would not have been enough says Turok

Ben
No ways! No experience- It’s the same as Phiyega…honestly I think its irresponsible

Link
No matter how bad the news gets until now we have always known that the treasury was sacrosanct – well minister Nene’s removal as the gatekeeper, signalled a line had been crossed and it evoked fury across South Africa

Zuma must go! Zuma must go!

My message to you Mr president we are tired and to the NEC stop protecting Zuma – we see you – we put you there and we gonna take you out of there

Business Day Editor Songezo Zibi says Treasury is being reigned in because it holds the line
Songezo Zibi
What the president did is to demonstrate that the treasury can be attacked and after that we only have the reserve bank and there will be nothing left afterwards

Commentary Five
Enough is enough, said enraged South Africans. #zumamustfall, became a rousing chorus on social media that later spilled out onto the streets

Vox One
We have a simple message for JZ: South Africa comes first not his political party

Commentary six
Minister Nene had stood up to SAA board chairperson Dudu Myeni – friend of the president and head of the Jacob Zuma foundation. She refused to accept an airbus swop arrangement that would save SAA money. He sent a letter warning that failure to do the deal by tomorrow would be considered financial misconduct. Shortly afterwards he was out

Bongani
How much pressure then was Minister Nene under?
Songezo
He was under enormous pressure – SAA was simply the straw that broke the camels back

Link
So what was the real reason for minister Nene’s removal – was it his ultimatum to the president’s friend at SAA? Or was it the nuclear procurement deal? Either way very few believe the official line – that he was freed up for the BRICS bank position

Commentary Seven
Nene had also publicly stated that the nuclear procurement programme would not go ahead if we couldn’t afford it. Only hours before he was sacked – the cabinet approved the nuclear programme without a cost benefit analysis.

Songezo
This is going to cost us upwards of 1.5 trillion now if there is no money for SAA where are we going to get money for nuclear

Commentary eight
Yet in his post cabinet briefing to journalists minister in the presidency Jeff Radebe failed to mention the cabinet approval for the procurement process to begin

Songezo
I think it’s a helluva thing to forget! I don’t think he forgot by the way – I think
they understood fully well that the consequent question would be where will you get the money, and there would be no answers

Commentary nine
Zibi also punches holes in the Presidents BRICS Bank explanation

Songezo Zibi
That statement is nonsense! We are two months away from the next budget – who removes a finance minister for a position that wont be filled until after that. But there is another thing Bongani – the board of the development bank has not approved the position – no other country that has nominated anyone for this position – and so the president selling us a story

Commentary ten
A story no one believed – especially the markets. Economist George Glynos was astounded and watched the rand dive almost 10% and savings wiped out overnight

George
Just looking at the numbers on the JSE and the Bond market you could come up with figures north of R200 billion that was wiped off in the space of a couple of days

Commentary eleven
So now we speak in Nkandlas- one analyst calculated that in only two days R500billion was wiped out of the economy– that could buy 2000 Nkandlas, one every day, for the next five years.

George Glynos
We are speaking about real people through pension funds …that will have taken a helluva beating

Commentary twelve
Minister Lindiwe Zulu is on the ANC National working committee that has come out defending the president

Bongani
Minister the ANC has defended this decision saying…can only be valid if they are rational?

Lindiwe Zulu
Yes this was a rational decision …because once the president had indicated opportunity of Nene going to BRICS bank that is a serious position – but its his prerogative because what are you a president if you cant take decisions

George Glynos
It might have been his prerogative but it doesn’t make it the right decision. It was just bad it was catastrophic in some instances and so accountability needs to be had in this instance, and I would like it in the form of the president stepping down.


Commentary Fourteen
And that was the message on the streets on Reconciliation day. In Cape Town Mpho Tutu relayed her famous father’s sentiments

MPHO TUTU
He is incredibly saddened by the events of the last few weeks and by the callous disregard for public good that is demonstrated by the current administration

Up sound Singing

Vavi
We are up to here with their corruption

Commentary fifteen
Zwelenzima Vavi was one of several eminent persons to sign an open letter to the President he was once close to

Bongani
When he made the decision to fire Nene what was he thinking?

Vavi
He is too powerful, his people love him, only a few cleva blacks will raise fingers, there will be a small hue and cry it will die down – it will be business as usual- to me this is a new ZUMA altogether

Commentary sixteen
As the markets bled, the ANC remained largely silent

Songezo
The ANC for days was paralysed! If it is paralysed from intervening in critical moments like this – you have to ask how much capacity they actually have if its own governance appears to be captured by interests outside of the ANC?

Commentary seventeen
Zibi points to the Gupta’s but they have denied any wrongdoing

Songezo
When a president is captured it means they become the de facto president and start appointing people in cabinet /That relationship is a danger to the stability and security of this country

Commentary eighteen
And Zwelenzima Vavi agrees

Vavi
I think the power of the ministers has been eroded over time by the Gupta factor behind the scenes-I think we have a dual power situation here



LINK
On Sunday afternoon the president was still defiant – then late on Sunday evening – the announcement came that Pravin Gordhan would now be the new finance minister. The banks stepped in and warned of a Monday morning blood bath

Commentary Nineteen
Bank shares had plunged an average of 18% and there were fears of a currency collapse

George
I think we could have been staring at a dollar rand that could have been substantially higher – possibly levels of 17 maybe 18 rand to the dollar – at that point you would talk about a central bank forced to raise interest rates to raise the value of the rand and you begin to realise this could have been quite disastrous

Commentary twenty
On Monday Pravin Gordhan moved quickly to assuage the country’s fears

Pravin Gordhan press conference
It is our duty to continuously earn the trust and confidence of the SA public and we commit ourselves to doing just that

Commentary twenty-one
But it was not enough for Moody’s, who downgraded our rating from stable to negative. George Glynos believes junk status is inevitable

George
We have heard today the ANC saying that fiscal policy hasn’t changed well that is part of the problem- its what has led to all the credit ratings downgrades that we have over recent years and what could very well lead us to JUNK going forward.

Commentary twenty-two
On Tuesday the ANC National working committee held an unconvincing press conference backing the president

Jessie Duarte
The president’s willingness to change an earlier deployment in the face of our sluggish economic climate demonstrated bold leadership bringing certainty
And assurance in the finance portfolio

Commentary Twenty -Three
They admitted the president was taken aback by the devastating backlash

Bongani
So doesn’t that suggest that he is out of his depth?


Minister Lindiwe Zulu
Absolutely not out of his depth but when he takes a decision and he realises the negative impact, he was man enough to stand up and say yes I am making a mistake and I would listen to what people are saying

Ben Turok
I can’t believe it for a minute – its just cover up. Some intervention happened at very high level, he would not have moved like that because of second thoughts. No way he is a stubborn man a strong man he would not have changed his mind that easily

Commentary Twenty- Two
Spare a thought for Des Van Rooyen, shuffled unceremoniously into local government portfolio only months before an election

Up sound Des
Our president has placed our country first and I echo JZ words that as a democratic government we must listen to our citizenry

Commentary Twenty-Three
The rand ended the week just above R15 to the dollar, but South Africa INC is now a risky place for investors. Expect 2016 to be expensive

SONGEZO ZIBI
There is no more space for mistakes, Bongani no more space for arrogance no more space for miscalculations – because when that happens we go to junk status and a lot of people in this country don’t remember when interest rates were 23% - you do not want junk status in this country Bongani!

2015 - Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 19 January 2016 Script: ZUMA’S BIGGEST BLUNDER FINAL SCRIPT 19th December 2015 FINAL Commentary One Last week ANC stalwart Ben Turok flew home, picked up a paper at the airport and read the news that had shocked South Africa President I have decided to remove Minister Nhalanhle Nene as minister of Finance…to another strategic position BEN TUROK I could hardly believe it, and I had to read several paragraphs and I was shocked and frankly upset know him well, He is a decent man of integrity -very hard working Commentary Two Nene’s replacement Des Van Rooyen, an ANC backbencher was also the convener of the economic cluster in parliament John: When you heard that he had been elevated to the position what was your response Ben Turok Disbelief and Irritation, even annoyance because I have had a lot to do with Des Van Rooyen. It was clear to me that he spent his whole parliamentary life working on his studies instead of on parliament. Commentary Three Van Rooyen has a masters degree in finance but that would not have been enough says Turok Ben No ways! No experience- It’s the same as Phiyega…honestly I think its irresponsible Link No matter how bad the news gets until now we have always known that the treasury was sacrosanct – well minister Nene’s removal as the gatekeeper, signalled a line had been crossed and it evoked fury across South Africa Zuma must go! Zuma must go! Up sound My message to you Mr president we are tired and to the NEC stop protecting Zuma – we see you – we put you there and we gonna take you out of there Commentary Four Business Day Editor Songezo Zibi says Treasury is being reigned in because it holds the line Songezo Zibi What the president did is to demonstrate that the treasury can be attacked and after that we only have the reserve bank and there will be nothing left afterwards Commentary Five Enough is enough, said enraged South Africans. #zumamustfall, became a rousing chorus on social media that later spilled out onto the streets Vox One We have a simple message for JZ: South Africa comes first not his political party Commentary six Minister Nene had stood up to SAA board chairperson Dudu Myeni – friend of the president and head of the Jacob Zuma foundation. She refused to accept an airbus swop arrangement that would save SAA money. He sent a letter warning that failure to do the deal by tomorrow would be considered financial misconduct. Shortly afterwards he was out Bongani How much pressure then was Minister Nene under? Songezo He was under enormous pressure – SAA was simply the straw that broke the camels back Link So what was the real reason for minister Nene’s removal – was it his ultimatum to the president’s friend at SAA? Or was it the nuclear procurement deal? Either way very few believe the official line – that he was freed up for the BRICS bank position Commentary Seven Nene had also publicly stated that the nuclear procurement programme would not go ahead if we couldn’t afford it. Only hours before he was sacked – the cabinet approved the nuclear programme without a cost benefit analysis. Songezo This is going to cost us upwards of 1.5 trillion now if there is no money for SAA where are we going to get money for nuclear Commentary eight Yet in his post cabinet briefing to journalists minister in the presidency Jeff Radebe failed to mention the cabinet approval for the procurement process to begin Songezo I think it’s a helluva thing to forget! I don’t think he forgot by the way – I think they understood fully well that the consequent question would be where will you get the money, and there would be no answers Commentary nine Zibi also punches holes in the Presidents BRICS Bank explanation Songezo Zibi That statement is nonsense! We are two months away from the next budget – who removes a finance minister for a position that wont be filled until after that. But there is another thing Bongani – the board of the development bank has not approved the position – no other country that has nominated anyone for this position – and so the president selling us a story Commentary ten A story no one believed – especially the markets. Economist George Glynos was astounded and watched the rand dive almost 10% and savings wiped out overnight George Just looking at the numbers on the JSE and the Bond market you could come up with figures north of R200 billion that was wiped off in the space of a couple of days Commentary eleven So now we speak in Nkandlas- one analyst calculated that in only two days R500billion was wiped out of the economy– that could buy 2000 Nkandlas, one every day, for the next five years. George Glynos We are speaking about real people through pension funds …that will have taken a helluva beating Commentary twelve Minister Lindiwe Zulu is on the ANC National working committee that has come out defending the president Bongani Minister the ANC has defended this decision saying…can only be valid if they are rational? Lindiwe Zulu Yes this was a rational decision …because once the president had indicated opportunity of Nene going to BRICS bank that is a serious position – but its his prerogative because what are you a president if you cant take decisions George Glynos It might have been his prerogative but it doesn’t make it the right decision. It was just bad it was catastrophic in some instances and so accountability needs to be had in this instance, and I would like it in the form of the president stepping down. Commentary Fourteen And that was the message on the streets on Reconciliation day. In Cape Town Mpho Tutu relayed her famous father’s sentiments MPHO TUTU He is incredibly saddened by the events of the last few weeks and by the callous disregard for public good that is demonstrated by the current administration Up sound Singing Vavi We are up to here with their corruption Commentary fifteen Zwelenzima Vavi was one of several eminent persons to sign an open letter to the President he was once close to Bongani When he made the decision to fire Nene what was he thinking? Vavi He is too powerful, his people love him, only a few cleva blacks will raise fingers, there will be a small hue and cry it will die down – it will be business as usual- to me this is a new ZUMA altogether Commentary sixteen As the markets bled, the ANC remained largely silent Songezo The ANC for days was paralysed! If it is paralysed from intervening in critical moments like this – you have to ask how much capacity they actually have if its own governance appears to be captured by interests outside of the ANC? Commentary seventeen Zibi points to the Gupta’s but they have denied any wrongdoing Songezo When a president is captured it means they become the de facto president and start appointing people in cabinet /That relationship is a danger to the stability and security of this country Commentary eighteen And Zwelenzima Vavi agrees Vavi I think the power of the ministers has been eroded over time by the Gupta factor behind the scenes-I think we have a dual power situation here LINK On Sunday afternoon the president was still defiant – then late on Sunday evening – the announcement came that Pravin Gordhan would now be the new finance minister. The banks stepped in and warned of a Monday morning blood bath Commentary Nineteen Bank shares had plunged an average of 18% and there were fears of a currency collapse George I think we could have been staring at a dollar rand that could have been substantially higher – possibly levels of 17 maybe 18 rand to the dollar – at that point you would talk about a central bank forced to raise interest rates to raise the value of the rand and you begin to realise this could have been quite disastrous Commentary twenty On Monday Pravin Gordhan moved quickly to assuage the country’s fears Pravin Gordhan press conference It is our duty to continuously earn the trust and confidence of the SA public and we commit ourselves to doing just that Commentary twenty-one But it was not enough for Moody’s, who downgraded our rating from stable to negative. George Glynos believes junk status is inevitable George We have heard today the ANC saying that fiscal policy hasn’t changed well that is part of the problem- its what has led to all the credit ratings downgrades that we have over recent years and what could very well lead us to JUNK going forward. Commentary twenty-two On Tuesday the ANC National working committee held an unconvincing press conference backing the president Jessie Duarte The president’s willingness to change an earlier deployment in the face of our sluggish economic climate demonstrated bold leadership bringing certainty And assurance in the finance portfolio Commentary Twenty -Three They admitted the president was taken aback by the devastating backlash Bongani So doesn’t that suggest that he is out of his depth? Minister Lindiwe Zulu Absolutely not out of his depth but when he takes a decision and he realises the negative impact, he was man enough to stand up and say yes I am making a mistake and I would listen to what people are saying Ben Turok I can’t believe it for a minute – its just cover up. Some intervention happened at very high level, he would not have moved like that because of second thoughts. No way he is a stubborn man a strong man he would not have changed his mind that easily Commentary Twenty- Two Spare a thought for Des Van Rooyen, shuffled unceremoniously into local government portfolio only months before an election Up sound Des Our president has placed our country first and I echo JZ words that as a democratic government we must listen to our citizenry Commentary Twenty-Three The rand ended the week just above R15 to the dollar, but South Africa INC is now a risky place for investors. Expect 2016 to be expensive SONGEZO ZIBI There is no more space for mistakes, Bongani no more space for arrogance no more space for miscalculations – because when that happens we go to junk status and a lot of people in this country don’t remember when interest rates were 23% - you do not want junk status in this country Bongani! THE END 12 05 In at 00 01 00 00 Out at 00 13 05 Duration 12 05 Promo one in at 00 13 30 00 Promo Two in at 14 00 Promo three at 14 30 PROMO ONE 15 seconds How many Nkandla’s could we buy with the money wiped out of the economy After finance minister Nhlanhla Nene was recalled George You could come up with figures north of R200 billion that was wiped off in the space of a couple of days PROMO TWO 15 seconds Did the President listen to the people when he changed his mind about the finance minister? Ben Turok I can’t believe it for a minute – its just cover up. He would not have moved like that because of second thoughts. No way. PROMO THREE 10 seconder The president’s dismissal of finance minister Nhlanhla Nene sent the currency into free fall, banking shares plunged and millions of our savings were wiped out.
